items.caption: înghețată cu aromă de cacao
items.rationale: Accept as a named cocoa-flavored ice-cream variant. The Cuisinart recipe uses cocoa powder in its chocolate ice cream; JamilaCuisine independently includes cocoa in the mixture. Gourmandelle explicitly assigns the chocolate flavor to cocoa. The noun phrase selects that flavor and does not claim that all ice cream contains cocoa, or that cocoa is an artificial flavoring. Only Cacao to Inghetata is traversable; the absent reverse must stay unavailable.

items.caption: chec în variantă cu cacao
items.rationale: JamilaCuisine includes cocoa in its chec recipe and explicitly permits omitting it. The qualifier in varianta therefore preserves the optional nature of cocoa instead of making it definitional for all chec. Only Cacao to Chec is traversable; the pair wording does not authorize the reverse.

items.caption: înghețată în variantă cu lapte
items.rationale: The Cuisinart vanilla and chocolate ice-cream recipes and JamilaCuisine chocolate ice cream use milk. Gourmandelle supplies a concrete dairy-free counterexample, so in varianta cu lapte is necessary and factually accurate. The same noun phrase remains true for both existing traversals: it names a milk-containing version without asserting that milk is made from ice cream.

items.caption: chec servit alături de lapte
items.rationale: JamilaCuisine describes eating slices of chec alongside a glass of milk; its separate cherry-chec recipe also lists milk as an accompaniment. This supports a serving option, not a required ingredient, universal custom or exclusive pairing. The phrase describes chec served that way. Only Chec to Lapte is traversable; no reverse edge is inferred.
